The [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] had an '''apartment''' in [[Tipoca City/Legends|Tipoca City]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]].<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" /> Fett used the apartment as a safehouse for him and his son, [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]].<ref name="aotcvis">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> The apartment was hard to find within the city due to its lack of distinguishing features.<ref name="FF">[[The Official Star Wars Fact File 96|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' 96]]</ref>
{{Loc-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|We didn't want it to look like something from the Land of the Giants.|Peter Walpole|<ref name="Insider80">{{InsiderCite|80|Set Piece|Technical Readout: Jango Fett's Apartment}}</ref>}}
Jango Fett's apartment was created for the [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']]. A purposely subtle sizing difference was created with the molded black settee and other furniture pieces where they were built slightly higher than average so that a human's legs would not touch to ground when seated. To serve as a visual tie-in to the white armor of the [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] and the [[Stormtrooper/Legends|Stormtroopers]] of the [[original trilogy]] of ''[[Star Wars]]'' films, the apartment was given a lack of color. The scenes in the apartment were filmed in the last week of [[July]] [[2000]], on a soundstage at [[Fox Studios, Sydney]]. At the entrance of the set, a sign for non-actors was posted reading ''Please Use Bootes Provided When Walking on Set''.<ref name="Insider80" />
